item.title: Three fan-favorite Batman movies are being re-released in theaters next week in celebration of Batman Day.
item.description:
Three fan-favorite Batman movies are being re-released in theaters next week in celebration of Batman Day.
Warner Bros. has announced some big plans for Batman Day next week, one of which includes a whole weekend of Batman films in theaters. The studio will be re-releasing Tim Burton's Batman, Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, and The LEGO Batman Movie at participating AMC, Cinemark, and Regal theaters. However, feel free to check other chains as well; I also found a few smaller theaters playing some of these films.
The rollout will begin on Friday, September 18, with one movie playing each night throughout the weekend. According to listings, Batman will play on September 18, Mask of the Phantasm will screen on September 19, and The LEGO Batman Movie will be shown on September 20. In the past, theaters have shown Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy during this period, but that doesn't appear to be the case this year. Instead, TNT will be airing the trilogy on TV on September 19, and of course, they'll also be available to stream on HBO Max.
While most fans have likely seen Burton's Batman at some point in their lives, it's worth seeing big and loud in a movie theater, if given the opportunity. Batman: Mask of the Phantasm is also well worth seeing in theaters, as it had a theatrical release back in the 90s, but not many people actually made it to the theater to check it out. It's arguably one of the best Batman films out there, and if you haven't seen it at all, there's no better way to experience it than on the big screen.
In related news, Batman's next big-screen adventure is still a ways off. The Batman Part 2 starring Robert Pattinson is officially filming throughout the rest of the year and will hit theaters in February 2027, after years of production delays. The film's plot and villains are being kept under wraps, but Sebastian Stan is heavily rumored and speculated to play Harvey Dent/Two Face.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.
item.description:
The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.
The late, great Jacques still has one more ace up his sleeve. Orphans of Mossflower, the very last Redwall book penned by the celebrated British author, will be released posthumously alongside the saga’s first-ever box set next year.
As spotted by a post on the official Redwall fan Wiki, the digital publishing catalog platform Edelweiss features a frontlist of forthcoming Redwall books, which includes Orphans of Mossflower. As told by the frontlist, this will be the “final book in the series.”
Nothing else about the title was shared, but it’s expected to be a direct sequel to the series’ most recent book, The Rogue Crew — which was published in 2011, a whopping 15 years ago.
Jacques died that same year at 71 after suffering a heart attack. The Rogue Crew was the only Redwall book to be published after his death, meaning that Orphans of Mossflower will be the second. It’s unclear if any additions were made to the novel by his editors, or how far along it was at the time of his death — but we suspect we’ll learn the answers to these questions when it gets closer to being released next year.
For now, theories abound as to what adventures Mossflower's creatures will get up to in this last novel. One hypothesis points to the winner of a 2010 contest who got to create a character that would appear in a future Redwall novel. This character was initially suspected to be in The Rogue Crew, but that didn’t happen — and given that Jacques died shortly before it was published, fans are of the mind that this character might pop up in Orphans of Mossflower.
Speaking to those at the Redwall Wiki, the winner — named Olivia — said she created a haremaiden named Reisa Kartwell, explaining that "’Reisa’ comes from ‘reise,’ meaning ‘travel’ in German, and ‘Kartwell’ is derived from ‘karte,’ the German word for ‘map.’ Reisa is Salamandastron's cartographer, and her map depicting efficient travel paths proves invaluable when the Redwallers must quickly reach Salamandastron when Redwall is under attack.”
The Rogue Crew follows Abbot Thibb, the Longpatrol hares, and the titular rogue crew of sea otters as they defend Redwall Abbey from the vicious Razzid Wearat, who wreaks havoc on his wheeled ship that can traverse both land and sea. We’ll have to see where this story picks up in the final book when it’s published a year from now.
This news follows the sad cancellation of Netflix’s Redwall series earlier this year. Fans of animal-fantasy literature need not worry, though; Erin Hunter’s Warriors book saga is getting a long-awaited animated series on Disney+, as well as a video game, the latter of which will release in October 2026.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Writer-director Michael Mann is taking another crack at his 2006 film, Miami Vice. Miami Vice: Director’s Final Cut will make its world premiere at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 3, 2026.
item.description:
Writer-director Michael Mann is taking another crack at his 2006 film, Miami Vice.
It was announced today that Miami Vice: Director’s Final Cut will make its world premiere at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 3, 2026, followed by a Q&A with Mann.
It is described as “Michael Mann’s new cut” and that it will be shown in 4K. The Beyond Fest site doesn’t list the running time of this new cut.
If this version is truly a “new cut" then it will be an even different version of the film than the Miami Vice: Unrated Director’s Edition that was released on Blu-ray in 2008. The Unrated Director’s Edition is a re-edited film featuring scenes that were cut from the theatrical release as well as new music cues.
“These changes are enough to make this Miami Vice a slightly different and in some ways better experience than the theatrical cut, although the film's same fundamental flaws remain,” as I wrote in my review of the Unrated Director’s Edition at the time.
“This edition, however, is closer in tone to the TV series [which Mann exec produced but did not create], enough to have muted some of that criticism. For example, it opens with an offshore speedboat race set against the sunny Miami skyline and scored with electronic music, which conjures memories of the series' opening credits.”
Mann’s Miami Vice was a legendarily difficult production, culminating in the abrupt departure of lead actor Jamie Foxx, who played Detective Ricardo Tubbs opposite Colin Farrell as his partner, Sonny Crockett. Foxx abandoned the film during shooting in the Dominican Republic, a move that forced Mann to change the movie’s ending.
Although Miami Vice opened in first place at the domestic box office in 2006, it ultimately proved a commercial and critical misfire. However, the film has earned a cult status and critical reappraisal in the two decades since its release.
F1’s Joseph Kosinski will direct a big screen reboot, Miami Vice ‘85, that will star Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. That film will be released on May 19, 2028.

item.title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy has re-emerged, five years after its release, with a new Switch 2 version... and some fans hope it could lead to a sequel.
item.description:
Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy has re-emerged, five years after its release, with a new Switch 2 version... and some fans hope it could lead to a sequel.
During today's Nintendo Direct, fans were surprised to learn that Eidos Montreal's Guardians of the Galaxy game is coming back. It's getting a new "Encore Edition," exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2, which not only brings the game to a new platform, but also adds new content like special outfits for the cosmic heroes. This news came as a bit of a shock, since the game missed sales expectations despite having great reviews, so fans assumed that we'd never see this iteration of the Guardians ever again.
Now, this new release has some hoping that the Guardians may live on. Over on social media, excited fans are pleading to Marvel and Eidos Montreal to produce a sequel. Maybe a Switch 2 version could be used to test the waters, but it's hard to say. Either way, it's great to see such a beloved game finding its way back into the market, and hopefully, it can create some demand for another entry in the series.
"Don’t sleep on this game, Switch players. It’s fu**ing dope," said one fan. "Do yourself a favor and pick this up! It’s a GREAT game! I hate the fact that this gem got overlooked (and Midnight Suns as well btw)," noted another.
"Can we just get a sequel? The people have been asking for years," asked another fan. "Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy 2, please," another pleaded.
These are far from the only people asking for a sequel or begging new players to check it out; the comments under the announcement posts from Marvel Games and the game's official account are flooded with similar responses.
Guardians of the Galaxy has seemingly had legs over the years. A year after its release, the team behind the game announced it had reached 8 million players, partially thanks to the game's inclusion on services like Xbox Game Pass. It's unclear how many people have played it since then, but it's frequently deeply discounted, so the numbers have likely only grown a fair bit in the last four years. Eidos Montreal also stated that it had no regrets over the game, despite it not being a big seller.
Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition will hit Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. Whether it gets overshadowed by the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains to be seen, but hopefully it can find a new audience on the platform.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword dropped last week, and we’re of the opinion that it’s a 10/10 masterpiece.
If you’ve already jumped into the action or are generally curious about the story side of things, it's worth checking out the official companion webcomic. The story serves as a direct prequel to Way of the Sword, and is free to read for anyone with a Webtoon account.
The entire Onimusha series takes place in an alternate version of Japan’s feudal era. In the game’s canon timeline, Way of the Sword picks up over two decades after the previous mainline release, Dawn of Dreams, bringing the world of Genma into the Edo period.
The companion webcomic, subtitled "Fated Rivalry," picks up pretty soon before the main events of Way of the Sword. The story follows Miyamoto Musashi's rival, Sasaki Ganryu, who discovers an Oni Gauntlet on his vengeance-driven quest to become powerful enough to take down Musashi.
The prequel is being produced by Laurel Pursuit, a US-based studio that’s previously distributed the Dungeon Crawler Carl graphic novel as well as original webcomics like Defiance of the Fall. The Onimusha webcomic specifically features work from Webtoon creators jjolee, hilluhri, and BAEKSSE.
The first chapter was released this past Saturday and has amassed just over 20,000 clicks so far. Future chapters will continue to become available on Saturdays, though it’s unclear how long the full prequel webcomic will end up being.
Here’s the full description of the comic, which is free to read with a Webtoon account:
When you live by the way of the sword, there’s only room for one at the top.
Sasaki Ganryu has one goal: to become the strongest swordsman in the world. When a duel with the wandering samurai Miyamoto Musashi ends in humiliating defeat, Ganryu is consumed by rage. What follows is a bloody quest to reclaim his honor that leads him down a path of madness and obsession.
On his journey, he receives a mysterious artifact known as “The Oni Gauntlet”, that gives him a power no mortal blade could ever match. Hunting down ever-stronger foes has set him on a collision course to face off again against the only man who has ever bested him in battle.
A prologue to the latest game in Capcom’s iconic samurai action series: Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
This isn’t the first time Onimusha has extended beyond the gaming realm. A film based on the action series was pitched all the way back in the early 2000s, but was eventually canceled. What did eventually come to fruition was an anime adaptation, released on Netflix in 2023.
Most fans don’t consider that story canon to the games. The webcomic, in contrast, flows pretty much seamlessly into Way of the Sword while staying faithful to events from previous games in the series.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: The fighting game community is in the middle of a fierce debate over the amount of guest characters coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.
item.description:
The fighting game community is in the middle of a fierce debate over the amount of guest characters coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.
On September 9, SNK announced two more guest characters coming to City of the Wolves: Manjiro "Mikey" Sano and Ken "Draken" Ryuguji from Tokyo Revengers. These popular shonen anime protagonists mark the latest in a string of guest characters for the game, which include Chun-Li and Ken from Street Fighter, pro footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, music artist Salvatore Ganacci, and Kenshiro from Fist of the North Star.
That’s a lot of guest characters for a game that’s only a little more than a year old — and while Ken and Chun-Li make sense given Capcom and SNK’s wealth of crossovers over the years, five guest characters from totally unrelated franchises feels a bit excessive to some players (myself included).
There’s a trend sweeping through popular fighting games lately where non-fighting game characters are being included in major titles like Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8, and of course, City of the Wolves. For example, Final Fantasy 7’s Tifa Lockhart is coming to Street Fighter 6 next year, while Baki’s Yujiro Hanma is set to make a splash in Tekken 8 in 2027.
While these one-off characters aren’t ruffling too many feathers within the fighting game community (Tekken is a franchise known for including one or two oddball guests), the sheer amount of guest characters in CotW is raising eyebrows — especially given the fact that they don’t come from other fighting games.
“Lmfaoo, adding anything bruh. Kenshiro was dope, but what the f**k is this,” one player wrote on X.
“Funniest fighting game roster of all time bro,” another said.
“Love these two, but how did they get in over Baki, or hell, even Tokita Ohma?” another asked, referencing popular martial arts anime Kengan Ashura (which, funnily enough, celebrated a collaboration with Street Fighter 6 not long ago).
It’s worth noting that fighting games in general are no stranger to guest characters from totally different worlds; the Mortal Kombat franchise is perhaps the best example of this, having added characters like Robocop, Omni-Man, Homelander, the Terminator, Alien's Xenomorph, and many other similar fighters to its rosters over the years. However, the argument can be made that these additions followed a general theme in keeping with the Mortal Kombat vibe and universe, whereas City of the Wolves’ guests are all over the place (in fact, it’s the first time a real-life athlete has been put in a mainline fighting game — and what is Ronaldo doing in South Town, anyway?).
Whatever the case may be, SNK clearly sees a path forward with these guest characters, and I’m honestly intrigued where they’ll take the franchise next. Either way, the sheer amount of characters they’re adding to CotW per season is laudable… though not everyone is hyped for each fighter they’re putting out. (Speaking of which, can we get some more ladies on the roster?)

item.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve Brand Director Kazutoki Kono says developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.
item.description:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve brand director Kazutoki Kono joked that developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.
Kono visited China for the first time to answer questions in a group interview with the media following a hands-on demo for the game, where he opened up about how popular Tasha has become over the last few months.
The pink-haired pilot is a fan favorite, and the game hasn’t even come out yet; set to release on October 2, oodles of future players are already obsessed with Tasha Severskaya, a former “star pilot in Yuktobania's acrobatic team, Zvezda.” Tasha hopped aboard the Endurance to capture publicity footage, but the ensuing war kept her on the vessel, and now she’s part of the Joker Flight squad.
Speaking with the media, Kono admitted that he was surprised by how popular Tasha had become on social media, revealing that he’s personally on “Team Kate Evans,” the Lieutenant Commander and leader of Queen Flight. He also revealed that Tasha took the longest to develop out of any other character in the game, since the team kept tweaking different aspects of her design to make sure they got her just right.
“Work on Tasha started relatively early, and she was originally designed by a different artist. She is also the character that took the longest to finalize. Her story and direction were already set, but we kept modifying various aspects afterward, making her the character we refined the longest during development. That's why inside the development team, we jokingly call her 'the most expensive character,'” he said, per Invenglobal.
As for why she’s so popular, Kono thinks it has to do with her fashion sense, saying her pink hair and outfits reflect trends that are currently popular among fans.
“I think elements like her personality, outfit, and especially her sense of fashion in wearing military attire so uniquely happened to fit current trends well, which contributed to all the attention she received,” he explained.
We got the chance to preview Ace Combat 8 this summer, with IGN’s Will Borger saying it was a "very grounded game" that left him “satisfied, but knowing [he] still had so much more to do.” He also got to speak with the devs about their ambitious plans for the game’s multiplayer, which will include 100-player lobbies, several different mission types, and a co-op warfare mode.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve releases on October 2, 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam.

item.title: After years of it being rumored, Apple has finally revealed a foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo at the company's "Surprise and Shine" September event. Here's all the camera details, performance specs, and UI improvements Apple is packing into its newest device.
item.description:
After years of it being rumored, Apple has finally revealed a foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, at the company's "Surprise and Shine" September event.
Unlike other foldables, such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, the iPhone has the same aspect ratio in both folded and unfolded forms. When folded, the Duo has a 5.4-inch display – about the side of a passport – and unfolds to 7.6 inches. Both of these displays have a 1.4:1 aspect ratio – for context, that's in-between a 4:3 aspect ratio (equal to 1.34:1) and 16:9 (equal to 1.7:1).
Apple says it went with this format in order to maximize the usage of the larger, unfolded display. Most other foldables have a mostly-square shape when unfolded, which Apple points out wastes space to letterbox black bars when viewing traditional 16:9 content. The screen uses wide-angle OLEDs, and has a 3,000-nit peak brightness.
As with practically every foldable announcement in history, Apple says that it worked hard on eliminating the crease, and while we'll have to wait until we get our hands on it to say for sure, it seems like the company was successful. The iPhone Duo uses what Apple is calling a "nano-texture display" to maintain optimal screen-feel while doing what it needs to do in order to not have a visable crease. When unfolded, Apple says the Duo is the thinnest iPhone ever.
Powering this foldable iPhone is Apple's new A20 Pro chipset, the same found in the iPhone 18 Pro. With other foldables with flagship chipsets, you typically see slightly slower performance, especially in sustained workloads, because the phone ironically has less space to cool the chip. The iPhone Duo, meanwhile, utilizes a vapor chamber cooling system, but we'll have to wait for hands-on testing before passing judgement on how well it keeps things cool. More importantly, the A20 Pro chip is going to power both the internal and external display simultaneously, which means that there'll be essentially zero delay when swapping between screens.
The UI has been completely redesigned for the iPhone Duo, with primary controls and the dynamic island moved to the side of the screen. This should make things easier to access and activate when holding the phone in one hand. Plus, that aspect ratio mentioned above will give you more space to watch videos and play games, meaning the iPhone Duo has a shot at becoming the best foldable for gaming.
Apple showed off a variety of interesting use cases for the iPhone Duo. Standby mode works well here, as you can prop up a semi-folded Duo on your nightstand to serve as a bedside clock and alarm.
The camera system also gets some neat tricks. You can have the outer display preview the image, so your subject can see how your framing looks before the photo is taken – surely a boon for hapless Instagram partners everywhere. There's also a cool feature that lets you display a captivating animation, such as a clip of Snoopy dancing, in order to draw the attention of a child towards the camera. Meanwhile, Duo Facetime uses both the internal and external screens and cameras to let people on both sides of the device join a FaceTime call instead of having to crowd around a small screen and camera.
As for the camera itself, the main sensor is the same 48MP shooter as the iPhone 18 Pro, though it lacks the physical aperture shutter of that phone. Meanwhile, the internal camera is 12MP and sits under the display, remaining hidden until you need it.
Battery life is always a challenge on foldables, but Apple claims the iPhone Duo will be capable of "all-day" usage. That's an impressive claim, and one we'll surely be testing when we go hands-on with the device.
The iPhone Duo will be available in Night Sky (dark grey) and Star White colorways, and starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage, which is $100 less than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Preorders start on October 16, with the phone hitting store shelves on October 23.
For more on Apple's latest hardware, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, check out our roundup of everything announced at the September Apple event.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Attack on Titan is coming to theaters this fall, bringing the beginning of Hajime Isayama’s groundbreaking story and its harrowing end to 4DX and ScreenX cinemas in Japan.
item.description:
Attack on Titan is coming to theaters this fall, bringing the beginning of Hajime Isayama’s groundbreaking story and its harrowing end to 4DX and ScreenX cinemas in Japan.
September 9 has been officially recognized as Attack on Titan Day in Japan, and to celebrate, two movies compiling the first half of the iconic anime’s first season and its finale are coming to theaters. The catch is that these showings are only in Japan, and they aren’t your run-of-the-mill movie theaters; Attack on Titan Part 1: Guren no Yumiya is heading to cinemas for ScreenX, 4DX, and Ultra 4DX screenings.
If you’re familiar with 4DX, you’ll know that this is kind of wild. If you aren't, it’s a unique type of screening that takes place in theaters with special features like chairs that rumble, gusts of wind, water splashes, and other effects that make the viewing experience so immersive it’s like being on a theme park ride. (You’ve probably seen those viral videos from 4DX screenings of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey — they’re an intense thrill ride, and one that AoT fans won’t want to miss.)
Prepare to rappel off towers and roofs with the Scouting Legion’s 3D Maneuver Gear, flee from oncoming titans, and dodge flying debris — not to mention braving the steam that pours off of the Colossal Titan when it kicks through the walls of Shiganshina.
These screenings are listed for October 23, 2026, but don’t worry if you can’t make it to Japan in time to catch the show; Attack on Titan: The Last Attack, a film compilation of the series’ epic finale, is also coming to ScreenX cinemas in 2027, though no specific date has yet been listed.
ScreenX is different from 4DX in that it shows films on three panoramic screens, making it feel like viewers are totally surrounded by the action. We can only imagine how intense this type of screening will be for Eren’s terrifying final transformation and the all-consuming chaos of the Rumbling.
This is one of several fun activities planned for Attack on Titan fans. Taking inspiration from the Nine Titans, Kodansha is also organizing 99 special events, including making the first 99 chapters of the manga free on its Magapoke app for 99 hours ending on September 13.
Kodansha has even made an official YouTube channel specifically for Attack on Titan, which will host “exclusive content for fans worldwide, including limited-time anime streaming and special videos you won't find anywhere else.” Currently, it’s streaming episodes from Season 1 every Wednesday, though these are only available to viewers within Japan.
There’s a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks if you’re an Attack on Titan fan. This is the latest big news to come from the franchise after Eren’s English voice actor, Bryce Papenbrook, said he was so dedicated to convincingly selling one of the show’s most iconic moments that he literally unhinged his jaw to portray his character’s emotional pain.
In related news, Attack on Titan 3 was shown off at Summer Game Fest this year and is set for release this December. Like the games before it, players will be able to make their own character and experience the events of the Rumbling firsthand in this video game adaptation of the critically-acclaimed anime series.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: While I won't know exactly which devices Apple will show off at the event today, its a pretty safe assumption that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro are going to be there. There are also some strong rumors that Apple's long-expected foldable iPhone is going to make an appearance. After all, this will be the first Apple event helmed by the company's new CEO, John Ternus, so the company should have something big to mark the start of this new era.
item.description:
Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event just ended, and just like was rumored, the company finally revealed its first foldable, the iPhone Duo. Rather than taking cues from many of the existing foldables, Apple opted for a wider outer display, so that when the phone is unfolded, it has a more usable aspect ratio. That should help it become one of, if not the, best foldables for mobile gaming. The Duo will be out on October 23, so we'll have to wait a little longer for it, but it is more affordable than I thought it'd be, coming in at $1,999 for the 256GB model.
Of course, that wasn't the only iPhone Apple announced today. The iPhone 18 Pro was also shown off, and it's pretty much a straight spec bump from the iPhone 17 Pro, just with a larger vapor chamber, a slightly better camera and the A20 Pro powering it. That'll be available much earlier than the Duo, too, launching on September 18, starting at $1,199 and $1,299 for the Pro and Pro Max, respectively.
Both phones are focused a lot more on Apple Intelligence than previous phones, too, which is sure to be the most divisive part for most people. Still, it does seem like the company is focused on making Siri actually usable again, so hopefully the new model actually works the way it's intended. Siri stopped being useful for me basically as soon as the company shoved ChatGPT into it, after all.
The new AI models are being worked into the Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods 5, too, and it looks like Siri will be a much bigger part of both of those devices. Although, Apple did add 'Siri Recap' to the new Apple Watch, which is reminiscent of Copilot's Recall feature. Hopefully, Apple can avoid the security blunders that forced Microsoft to delay that feature when it first tried to roll it out in Windows 11.
I was live blogging the event, and the entire thing is included below, so you can see how this year's iPhone event played out in real time, without the trailers and cutaways that typically bloat Apple's events.
Times are in Eastern Daylight Time
2:15pm: I thought the iPhone Duo would have been more expensive, but it starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That's $100 less than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. You can preorder it on October 16, and get it October 23.
That's the whole show wrapped up, what a way to end it. The iPhone Duo looks incredible, and it isn't even as expensive as I feared it'd be. Can't wait to get my hands on it.
2:11pm: There are only two lenses on the iPhone Duo, rather than the three on the 18 Pro, but it has the same 48MP main shooter. But this isn't the type of phone you get if you want the best camera anyways, so I just look at this as a bonus.
2:08pm: The Duo is of course powered by the A20 Pro, but what's wild is that the chip is going to power both displays simultaneously, which should make for virtually no delay when you're swapping between the display modes. The difference between that and something like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 will probably be pretty hard to notice, but it's still cool. The Duo is also eSIM only, which lets the phone have a larger battery. Battery life is a massive pain point for foldables, but Apple claims that the phone can last up to 24 hours when using both display modes equally. That'd be huge if its true, and we'll just have to wait to see until it's out in the wild.
2:07pm: The iPhone Duo will have a nano-texture finish, that Apple claims minimizes the crease. That's something that every phone manufacturer has been trying to do for years, and while I can't see a crease in the footage so far, I'll only feel comfortable declaring Apple's success when I see it in person.
2:05pm: With that outer display's aspect ratio, the iPhone Duo really does remind me of the Surface Duo, just without the weird dual-screen design that Micrsoft's weird office-centric phone had. This will also come with the latest processor, which is something Microsoft was afraid to do with both iterations of its Duo.
2:00pm: Thank goodness, you'll be able to use the Apple Pencil on the Duo, so now I have an excuse to dig mine out of whatever drawer it's hiding in right now. The outer display apparently has 90% of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. The frame is reinforced with ceramic fibers, which, according to Apple, makes the Duo extremely durable, and it helps that it has an IP67 waterproof rating. Which is something that took other foldables years to achieve. That's the benefit of being seven years late to the foldable party, I guess.
1:59pm: Apple has a new UI for the Duo, and the dock is now vertical on the side of the screen, rather than the bottom, which should make it easier to open everything with a single hand, rather than needing to grip it with both hands. When the Duo is unfolded, it looks a lot like an iPad. It looks like the OS will react naturally to whatever state the phone is in, so you should be able to prop it open in a sort of L-shape and bring up a keyboard, like a mini laptop.
1:56pm: Apple is going with a bit of a wider aspect ratio for the outer display, which is apparently "the same size as your passport". That should make the aspect ratio of the inner display a bit more usable, which seems to be Apple's goal. And, unlike the 18 Pro, the camera is underneath the display with no dynamic island. When it's unfolded, Apple claims that the iPhone Duo is the thinnest iPhone yet.
1:54pm: One more thing. Here we go. John Ternus is introducing the first Apple Foldable. It is starting off with a trailer flying over a desert, and ended on the unfolded phone with what looks like a default Mac wallpaper. And here it is, the iPhone Duo.
1:51pm: Both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are available for preorder today, and launch on September 18. They'll cost the same as the Series 11 and Ultra 3, respectively at $399 and $799.
1:45pm: Now we're diving more into the AI capabilities of Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The first feature is 'audio intelligence', which will help you make sense of what you hear, which seems silly, but it can be helpful for anyone who's hard of hearing. The watch will notify you if something like a doorbell or a siren is detected. There's also a live rewind feature, where you can double tap the crown and get a transcription of what someone just said to you. That does likely mean that the Apple Watch is always listening to you, but I will admit that sometimes I zone out when someone is talking to me, so I can see the appeal here. And if you don't want the watch to listen to everything, you can turn Siri Recap off. And even if you leave it on, Apple promises that the recordings are only temporary and that Apple cannot access them.
1:42pm: The Health Sensing System will now give you a readiness report, just like the latest Pixel Watch, which will let you know when your body is ready for a rigorous workout. That way, you should be able to avoid unnecessary strain on your body. You can also order bloodwork from the Apple Watch, and the data from those tests will be uploaded to the Health app. I hope that's covered by insurance!
1:40pm: Now for the new Apple Watch 12 and Ultra 4, and of course Ternus is leading with how the Apple Watch will extend the reach of Apple Intelligence. The new watch has upgraded sensors, which make up a new "Health Sensing System." Background heart rate readings are now taken every 5 seconds, which is 60 times more frequently than the Apple Watch 11.
1:35pm: AirPods 5 is here, and it will of course have access to Siri AI, which will help you do things like live translation. And unlike the iPhone, it isn't going up in price, and will still start at $129 without noise cancelation. The new AirPods Pro is here too, with up to 5 hours of battery life with ANC enabled, and those will start at $149, which is $30 less than the last generation. Both will also be available on September 18.
1:31pm: The iPhone 18 Pro will be available for preorder on Saturday, and will be available to buy on September 18. It is more expensive than the 17 Pro, starting at $1,199, but it did say you could get it for $34.99 a month using the upgrade program. That's more expensive, but it's not as bad as I thought it'd be.
1:30pm: Apple is shrinking the dynamic island, but it doesn't seem like it's disappearing this year. I don't mind it, but I know a lot of people don't like having part of their screen cut out.
1:28pm: Apple is introducing 'Apple reference image,' which will have the camera digitally sign photos at the time of capture, so you know that it's not AI-generated. It'll also create a digital negative that can't be altered, so there's always a reference shot that you know hasn't been touched by AI.
1:23pm: The iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48mp main shooter, and it actually has a physical shutter, so you can adjust aperture beyond just software effects. This should be huge for shooting in low light, and could make the iPhone 18 Pro one of the best camera phones, but again, that's something I'll have to test when I actually get my hands on the phone. Apple is also introducting new pro controls, including white balance and lens aperture in the native camera app. Some of these photos look incredible, but professional photographers can take incredible pictures on pretty much any device, so that doesn't say much.
1:20pm: I'm excited to see how much battery life has improved. Apple claims that 5 minutes of charging will get you 6 hours of video playback. We'll see! Now we're looking at gaming on the 18 Pro, and Apple showed the phone running Monster Hunter Now, and it looked incredible. I'm going to have to check that one out.
1:18pm: Apple debuted its new vapor chamber on the 17 Pro, and it looks like there's a next-generation version of it on the 18 Pro. It has three times the surface area, which will hopefully make it a bit more effective. In my testing on the iPhone 17 Pro, the vapor chamber didn't actually impact sustained performance by much. Maybe it'll be different this year.
1:15pm: Apple Intelligence will be availble in 16 languages when the new iOS update launches later this month, and I have to admit I'm curious to see if it's actually good again. It's been a while. Now we're going to start looking at the A20 Pro, the new chipset. It has a 6-core CPU, with 2 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that the 'Super cores' are desktop class, which I'll have to wait and see when I test it. The A20 Pro also has a new 7-core GPU, each with a neural accelerator, which is how Siri AI will be running natively on the phone. There's also two seperate Neural engines built into the chip, which should make the iPhone 18 Pro incredibly strong for on-device AI work.
1:12pm: It looks like Siri AI will have much more customization for the voice. I can't stop thinking of that one scene from Companion where she's trying to steal the car.
1:10pm: Apple 18 Pro seems to be built around AI, which isn't super surprising, but the company is also launching 'Siri AI'. I hope this means Apple has its own model, instead of offloading the work onto ChatGPT like previous versions of the assistant. Unrelated, it doesn't look like the dynamic island is going anywhere this year.
1:08pm: Apple is kicking off the iPhone event with another trailer, featuring the moon and then zooming in on the A20 Pro, the chip that'll be powering the iPhone 18. "This is what happens when you go to the moon, come back and ask what's next".
1:05pm: Ternus is kicking off the event talking about a new smart hub for your phone, and I'm pretty sure he's going to use this AI talk to introduce the foldable. That "big screen" he mentioned is the big clue. Either way, he's positioning the iPhone as the "ultimate personal hub". Expect a lot of Apple Intelligence here.
1:02pm: The trailer then cut to Tim Cook, introducing John Ternus as the main character. And, well, yeah I guess he is at this point.
1:00pm: Here we go! Apple spent the last 15 minutes playing music over a vague blue and pink image, which turned out to be a super-zoomed in Apple logo. Surprising! Apple kicked things off with a man burning down what looks like a circus cart. There was also an old woman who peeled off her face to reveal a younger woman! This is quite the Apple event so far.
12:45pm: The show starts in 15 minutes, and we even have music playing! It's going to be the first Apple event with John Ternus headlining, and I half-expect a Tim Cook highlight reel to kick things off. I've been watching this iPhone event every year for more than a decade now, and I wonder if the structure is just going to feel exactly the same as it has for the last few years. At least I don't have to wait long to find out.
12:30pm: We're 30 minutes out, and I still don't know how I feel about the name "Surprise and Shine." I swear Apple finds the silliest way to name its big showcases. It's even funnier, because if the big surprise is the foldable iPhone, its one we all saw coming from a mile away at this point.
12:00pm: The event starts in about an hour, and I'm still not entirely sure what is going to be there. The rumors heavily suggest the foldable is going to be there, and Mark Gurman is even calling it the 'iPhone Duo' at Bloomberg. That just makes me think of the Microsoft Surface Duo (RIP).
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Callina Liang’s stunt double in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie had to wear butt pads in order to realistically match Chun-Li’s muscular physique.
item.description:
Callina Liang’s stunt double in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie had to wear butt pads in order to realistically match Chun-Li’s muscular physique.
Director Kitao Sakurai revealed this humorous anecdote during a Q&A session at a media event ahead of the movie’s official release. The topic was the intense training Liang underwent to achieve Chun-Li’s iconic thunder thighs, which grew her legs by 6.5 centimeters.
In fact, Liang’s silhouette had gotten so muscular that her stunt double couldn’t convincingly pull off her physique for action sequences — so she had to wear butt pads to make her glutes match the results of Chun-Li’s rigorous squat routine.
“I knew it was serious when we were filming a scene kind of later in the movie, and I saw Callina’s stunt double, and I was like, ‘What are you wearing?’ And there were like these butt pads that she had to wear just to match Callina’s physique,” Sakurai said.
Noah Centineo, who plays Ken Masters, chimed in: “Yeah, and then we had to wear them out of solidarity, too.”
“We all had huge legs,” Liang laughed.
Whatever it takes to become Chun-Li. 🫡 #StreetFighterMovie pic.twitter.com/NKDopb5iqT
Liang has been open about the work it took to bring Chun-Li to life, saying she took on a grueling martial arts routine and even ate a dozen eggs every single day to gain enough muscle mass.
"Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.
That’s not all; Liang also says she downloaded every version of Street Fighter available on her PlayStation 5 and recorded Chun-Li’s moves on her phone to get a better feel for how the First Lady of Fighting Games moves in battle.
Street Fighter releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. For more on the movie, you can check out our in-depth interview with David Dastmalchian, who plays the movie’s iconic villain, M. Bison, where he told us all about how he went on a deep dive into cult leaders throughout history to bring the psycho-powered dictator to life.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Apple has announced the iPhone 18 Pro at its 'Surprise and Shine' September event.
item.description:
Apple has just announced the iPhone 18 Pro at its 'Surprise and Shine' September event.
While last year's iPhone 17 Pro Max had a new chassis, with an improved camera shelf and a new vapor chamber, the iPhone 18 Pro has largely adopted the same design. Instead, Apple seems to be focusing on upping the spec, loading the phone with the new Apple A20 Pro processor, which is built on 2nm technology and the company claims to have 40% faster gaming performance than last year's model – though we'll be putting that claim to the test. It also packs in a second neural engine to effectively double performance in AI workloads.
Apple led the announcement touting the capabilities of Siri AI, showing things like email construction, system dictation, and camera integration, letting you ask questions about stuff you see in the wild, or pulling event details from a flyer and adding them to your calendar.
Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro uses a new vapor chamber for improved thermals. The battery is expected to match the iPhone 17 Pro Max – approximately 36 hours of video playback – while the iPhone 18 Pro Max will be capable of up to 45 hours. Apple claims that 5 minutes of charging will get you 6 hours of video playback.
Apple also discussed the phone's new camera capabilities. The iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48MP main camera featuring a physical shutter, which means that you can adjust the aperture manually beyond what's capable in software effects. In particular, this should make the camera excellent for shooting in low light settings.
This might not be the most exciting followup in Apple's history, so it doesn't help that it also comes with a higher price tag. Apple is charging $1,199 for the iPhone 18 Pro to start, compared to $1,099 for the 17 Pro, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299. Apple did avoid raising prices on the 17 Pro throughout the ongoing RAM crisis so far, so it seems to have been waiting for this new model. Still, the $100 price jump is less extreme than some other devices, so it seems like Apple is absorbing some of the cost of RAM, at least for now.
Preorders start on September 12, with the phone on store shelves on September 18.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: A massive sinkhole has opened up near the ocean in Malibu, California, threatening to swallow up the home of Hollywood star Nicolas Cage.
item.description:
A large sinkhole has opened up in the Californian city of Malibu, and is threatening to swallow up the home of Hollywood star Nicolas Cage.
The driveway at the front of the property, which reportedly belongs to the National Treasure, Con Air, and Face/Off star, has already fallen below ground. This is due to the approximately 30-by-30-foot sinkhole having emerged after heavy rainfall in the area.
On Monday, the hole had been estimated at around 8ft in size, with residents living nearby telling Los Angeles Magazine that, "at that point, the homeowners were not overly concerned. We thought it could be fixed pretty quickly."
But then "all hell broke loose."
On Tuesday morning, the gap opened up to nearer 30 feet in size, with emergency services being called to the area to attend to a gas leak caused by the event. This widening of the sinkhole is what caused the home’s driveway to collapse, with the building now exposed to further damage.
At least five homes on the street are said to have been deemed unsafe for entry by Malibu City officials, with access limited and the area described as "impassable due to the large portion of the road that has collapsed."
According to the New York Times, Cage bought the property only two years ago for a price of $10.5 million. It stands on stanchions rooted into the oceanbed it mostly hangs over, and it's due to the impact of powerful waves and heavy rain following a hurricane warning that the sinkhole is believed to have started.
Thankfully, no injuries have been reported due to the damage caused.
Nicolas Cage recently insisted that it’s "perfect" that one of his latest projects, Spider-Noir, will only be getting one season's worth of episodes. The Prime Video Spider-show was recently canceled by Amazon after viewing figures were shown to have dropped off after an initially strong start. Since its cancellation, Spider-Noir went on to earn five awards at the Creative Arts Emmys.
"For me, one season is perfect, having said what I wanted to say with this dangerous, innovative, pop-art Spider-Man," Cage told Deadline. "Onwards, upwards, inwards." Here's hoping the sinkhole is sorted before anything else heads inwards as well.
Image credits: David Swanson/AFP via Getty Images, Michael Loccisano/Getty Images.
Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social.

item.title: A brand new look at Spyro: A Realm Beyond has been shown off for the game's 28th anniversary.
item.description:
A brand new look at Spyro: A Realm Beyond has been shown off for the game's 28th anniversary.
The legendary purple dragon is finally making his return after being absent for nearly 20 years. Outside of a collection of remakes in 2018, Spyro hasn't had a brand new standalone adventure since 2008, but he will make his grand return next year. To celebrate the franchise's 28th anniversary, Activision has revealed a new look at the game with some artwork of a key location in Spyro: A Realm Beyond.
The artwork depicts one of the earliest regions players will explore, Arcadian Vale. The location is a calm, serene, and vibrant plane for Spyro to soar through. It's filled with ancient-looking stone structures, waterfalls, and sprawling grassy vistas.
"From curious critters to cheerful fodder creatures, no detail of Arcadian Vale is too small," reads an excerpt from a blog post about the new location. "Every corner captures the same sense of warmth, whimsy, and personality that fans have come to love and expect from Spyro and his universe. The Toys for Bob team have paid special attention to creating a charming world that feels inviting at every scale, all the way down to its smallest inhabitants."
Developer Toys for Bob also took this anniversary as an opportunity to thank fans for their passion for Spyro over the years. The studio also created a birthday cake, which featured a new look at Spyro and his supporting cast in A Realm Beyond.
"Your unwavering enthusiasm, passion, and creativity have helped to keep Spyro soaring through the years," Toys for Bob said. "Whether you’ve been here since the original trilogy, revisiting favorite moments in the Reignited Trilogy, sharing fan art, creating content, or introducing new players to Spyro’s world, this community has always been at the heart of the franchise."
Spyro was a staple of the late 1990s and early 2000s, along with the likes of Crash Bandicoot. The two emerged as iconic platforming legends and both were created by teams that would go on to become prestigous PlayStation-owned studios. Crash Bandicoot was created by Naughty Dog, while Spyro was molded by Insomniac Games. Both franchises eventually got handed off to different developers, before being acquired by Activision in 2008.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Sony has confirmed the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for September 2026, which is headlined by RuneScape: Dragonwilds, WWE 2K26 and Ball x Pit.
item.description:
Sony has confirmed the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for September 2026, which is headlined by RuneScape: Dragonwilds, WWE 2K26 and Ball x Pit.
Indie romance simulator Date Everything!, suspenseful adventure Slitterhead and Ninja Gaiden: Ragebound are also all worth a look. A personal favorite this month, though, is Dungeons of Hinterberg — a brilliant game that mixes the puzzles of Zelda with the forging of small town relationships through daily interactions with the locals.
Rounding out the selection this month is long-range shooter Sniper Elite: Resistance, while PlayStation Premium subscribers gain access to retro RPG Mega Man X Command Mission and Metro Redux.
Once again, it's worth remembering that Sony is still experimenting with the timing of new PS Plus game releases in some countries, which means the games will be released on varying dates throughout the month if you're in the U.S., the UK and Japan. The full lineup will be available to play on September 15 in all other regions.

item.title: The remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 are coming to Nintendo Switch 2 next month.
item.description:
The remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 are coming to Nintendo Switch 2 next month.
Capcom is making sure fans can enjoy classic Resident Evil games on the go by porting the trilogy of remakes over to Nintendo Switch 2. The games were announced for the console durign today's Nintendo Direct and will arrive digitally on October 16, with physical versions to follow on in January 2027.
These won't be sold exclusively as a collection (though it wouldn't be surprising if there is a bundle), so fans will be able to pick which ones they want to purchase and play.
Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 will come with their respective DLCs, including 4's Separate Ways expansion that follows Ada Wong. No other unique features or upgrades were mentioned, so don't expect any radical changes if you've already played these remakes elsewhere. Nevertheless, it's a great offering for those who either want to revisit them portably or play them for the first time.
The bulk of the mainline, numbered Resident Evil games will be natively available on the platform once these release, as Capcom previously released Resident Evil 7, Village, and Requiem for the console. Of course, we're still missing native versions of Resident Evil 1, 5, and 6, but all three of those games are available on Switch 1 and playable on Switch 2 through the console's backward compatibility. As a result, fans can play the entire Resident Evil saga on Switch 2, which is nothing to scoff at.
The next Resident Evil remake will be for Code Veronica. The game — now just Resident Evil Veronica — was announced at Summer Game Fest, though details are still relatively scarce on the project. It is currently scheduled to be released next year and, yes, it will also launch for Nintendo Switch 2.
Catch up on all of the big announcements in our roundup of everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast, as well as everything announced in The Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct that aired yesterday.

item.title: Nintendo has revealed Kirby and the World Beyond with a first-look gameplay trailer ahead of its launch on Nintendo Switch 2.
item.description:
Nintendo has revealed Kirby and the World Beyond with a first-look gameplay trailer ahead of its launch on Nintendo Switch 2.
In what will almost surely come as a surprise to Super Smash Bros., Nintendogs, and even Kirby fans everywhere, everyone’s favorite powerful pink hero closed out today’s September 2026 Nintendo Direct. This first look at Kirby and the World Beyond came with an early look at gameplay, showing that, per usual, Kirby will be able to use his copy abilities to slay foes.
This looks like a much more open adventure than Nintendo has offered in the past. In fact, Kirby and the World Beyond might be Kirby’s most open experience yet when it launches for Nintendo Switch 2 spring 2027.
"A new 3D adventure is on the horizon for Kirby!" Nintendo confirmed in a press release. "Freely explore an expansive world and put Kirby’s Copy Abilities to creative use as you uncover what awaits in Kirby and the World Beyond."
As noted during the Direct, Kirby and the World Beyond's spring 2027 launch for Switch 2 just so happens to coincide with the franchise's 35th anniversary. Nintendo's Yoshiaki Koizumi promised that more details on this front will be shared "in the future."
It's been a while since we got a proper new Kirby game. Aside from spinoffs like 2025's Kirby Air Riders and reimaginings like 2023's Kirby's Return to Dreamland Deluxe, the last mainline installment in the classic Nintendo franchise arrived with Kirby and the Forgotten Realm when it launched for the original Switch in early 2022.
With a fresh look at a new, more open world and refreshed copy-ability gameplay, fans have already begun to imagine how this next new game will take the series forward. Part of that has seen some drawing comparisons between Kirby's world-hopping antics and Jim Carrey's 1998 film, The Truman Show.
They put Kirby in the Truman show pic.twitter.com/y06tfl8CBH
kirby and the world beyond pic.twitter.com/OeLExIjtTL
It sounds like there are big plans in store for Kirby, but we'll have to wait to see what's in store. Until there's more to share about Kirby and the World Beyond, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review for the Kirby and the Forgotten Land Star-Crossed World re-release.

item.title: Nintendo has revealed that a Mario Kart World update will add classic SNES tracks, Knockout Tour courses, and more later today.
item.description:
Nintendo has revealed that a Mario Kart World update will add classic SNES tracks, Knockout Tour courses, and more today.
The company announced the news as part of its September 2026 Nintendo Direct today. While there are no new playable characters or outfits in Mario Kart World (yet), the new update should arrive as a welcome surprise to players who have been looking for a reason to grab the wheel following its Nintendo Switch 2 launch last summer.
A total of 10 classic courses have been added as part of the update. As a bonus, these courses feature old-school item tiles instead of the flashier floating boxes. For the Knockout Tour courses, players can look forward to two new routes to race through.
A free update for Mario Kart World launches later today!Play 10 classic courses from Super Mario Kart in VS Race mode and two new Knockout tour routes. #NintendoDirectGet the update: https://t.co/K9I0I75Mhh pic.twitter.com/1FIL2jzzQY
"Classic courses from Super Mario Kart have been hiding in plain sight across the continent of Mario Kart World, and now 10 of them can be played as standalone races in VS Race," Nintendo said in a press release. "Tear through Choco Island, Vanilla Lake, Ghost Valley and more, complete with ? Panels that grant items just like in the Super NES original. The update also adds two new Knockout Tour routes, Propeller Rally and Turnip Rally, plus a Spectator Mode when playing with friends online or via LAN Play."
Everything shown during today's Nintendo Direct trailer will arrive when Mario Kart World update 1.8.0 launches free for Switch 2 players later today. Patch notes for the update are already available, so you can see the full list of every classic track joining with the update below.

item.title: Samus Aran will return in Metroid Ravenous, a side-scrolling sequel to Metroid Dread.
item.description:
Samus Aran will return in Metroid Ravenous, a side-scrolling follow-up to Metroid Dread.
Announced during today's Nintendo Direct broadcast, Metroid Ravenous will launch for Switch 2 on January 28, 2027, priced at $59.99 for a digital copy — the same as Nintendo's upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
A debut trailer for the game revealed Samus being attacked by strange enemies who zapped her energy. "It's eat or be eaten," she says in response. Hope you're hungry.
It’s eat…or be eaten. #MetroidRavenous. 28/01/2027. Only on #NintendoSwitch2. pic.twitter.com/b7f9fQWRmo
"I was attacked by unknown assailants and sustained grave injuries," Samus says in the Metroid Ravenous reveal trailer. "I don't know where I am, getting back to the surface won't be easy. My chances of getting off this moon are slim at best. Still... I will survive. And I will make it home. Even if I have to feed on my enemies to do so. It's eat or be eaten."
If the game's name sounds familiar, that's because Metroid Ravenous popped up this summer via a swiftly-deleted ratings board listing in Brazil. At the time, fans speculated that its name referred to Dread's main antagonist Raven Beak.
Ravenous appears to once again be the work of talented Spanish development studio MercurySteam, the team that previously collaborated with Nintendo for Metroid Dread, as well as Metroid: Samus Returns, the remake of Game Boy title Metroid 2: Return of Samus for 3DS.
"A surprise sequel after nearly 20 years, Metroid Dread brings back the legendary exploration and progression and merges it with excellent modern combat and some of the best boss fights ever," we wrote in IGN's Metroid Dread review, scoring it a 9/10.
For the uninitiated, Nintendo's side-scrolling Metroid games are narratively separated from its first-person Metroid Prime subseries, though all part of the same overall franchise. Dread and Ravenous sit at the end of the series' chronology to date, years after the events of last year's Metroid Prime 4, so don't expect any direct continuation of that.
Also announced today: the Metroid Ravenous amiibo collection, which will include individual Samus and Chozo Statue figures. A third amiibo, Samus (Metroid Suit), will be bundled with Ravenous' Special Edition that includes the game and a SteelBook case.
Catch up on all of the big announcements in our roundup of everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast, as well as everything announced in The Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct that aired yesterday.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Viral hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon is sneaking onto Nintendo Switch 2 – and it’s out today.
item.description:
Viral hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon is sneaking onto Nintendo Switch 2 – and it’s out today.
The indie developer behind the popular PC video game, lemorion_1224, confirmed the news during today’s September 2026 Nintendo Direct. Instead of waiting to check out Meccha Chameleon with a later release date, it was confirmed that players will be able to paint themselves into the experience starting today.
It’s currently unclear if Meccha Chameleon will come to other platforms like PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
Paint yourself to blend in and trick the seekers. Can you stay hidden? 🎨🦎 MECCHA CHAMELEON is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 later today! #NintendoDirect @lemorion1224 pic.twitter.com/3rIxa2IVNQ
"Blend into your surroundings in this competitive multiplayer game that combines drawing and hide-and-seek," Nintendo said. shortly after its Direct reveal. "Strike a pose and paint yourself to become one with nearby walls, furniture, or ornaments using colors and patterns while the 'It' team searches for hidden players. Supporting 1-12 players online3, every match rewards creativity and quick thinking."
Meccha Chameleon launched for PC via Steam in June and quickly became one of the biggest games of 2026. Millions of copies sold and a few surprising collaborations later, lemorion's entertaining multiplayer game is still entertainment players despite its lack of a console release. It coming to Switch 2, however, will open the door for even more fans to try it out.
In case you're unaware, Meccha Chameleon has fans play a game of hide-and-seek where players are able to blend into environments by using their painting skills. It's easy enough for anyone to try but still has a high skill celing, with some of the more talented artists showing off the abilities by recreating the Mona Lisa.
